questions.question: Explainthesymmetryofflowerswithsuitableexamples. [K] / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Flower symmetry describes how the petals, sepals, and other floral parts can be divided into identical halves.
  • Three main types flowers are there based on their symmetry.
  • Actinomorphic (Radial Symmetry):
  • A flower that can be divided into two equal/identical halves along any vertical radial plane passing through the
  • center. e.g. Hibiscus, Allamanda, Ixora, etc
  • Zygomorphic (Bilateral Symmetry):
  • A flower that can be divided into two identical halves along only one single vertical plane passing through the
  • center. e.g. Clitoria, Crotalaria, Orchids, etc.
  • Asymmetric:
  • A flower that cannot be cut into two equal halves along any vertical plane through the center.
  • e.g. Canna indica.
